notes: THE NUMBERS ON THE SCREEN NOW MEAN WHAT THEY SAY. This release comes out of an audit that asked a different question from the usual one: not "is the entry right?" but "is what you are shown the same as what the books actually hold?" Five places were found where they differed. A DATED GENERAL LEDGER EXTRACT NOW OPENS WITH THE BALANCE BROUGHT FORWARD. Ask for one account from the first of February and the Balance column used to begin at zero, which quietly made it the movement for those weeks while still calling itself the balance. Against a cashbook of 250,140.00 the extract would read 12,340.00, and the difference — the opening balance — looked for all the world like an unexplained variance somebody would reach for a journal to correct. The extract now carries a Balance brought forward line, worked out over the same account, unit and project you filtered by, and it appears on the screen, on the print and in the Excel file alike. A BANK ACCOUNT HELD IN DOLLARS IS SHOWN IN CEDIS, AND SAYS SO. The dashboard took the cedi figure from the ledger and printed it with the account's own currency code, so an account holding ten thousand dollars read USD 125,000.00 — the dollar balance overstated twelvefold, on the first screen after you sign in. THE BUDGET METER NOW MEASURES THIS YEAR'S EXPENDITURE BUDGET. It had been dividing your spending by every budget line ever entered — previous years included, and income budgets alongside expenditure — so the meter could read comfortably within budget against a figure no one had ever approved. A BACK-DATED AGED LISTING CARRIES ITS WARNING INTO THE EXCEL FILE, which is the copy that gets filed as a working paper; the screen and the print already said it. And the Entries column in the notes counts postings rather than days, so twelve fuel payments on one date no longer show as one. THE ACCOUNT PICKER NOW WORKS FROM THE KEYBOARD. Every account, vendor, bank, unit and project field shares one picker, and its rows could be reached with the Tab key but only ever responded to the mouse — so you could land on an account, press Enter, and have nothing happen. Type to search, arrow to the line, Enter to choose, Escape to close. Nothing changes if you use the mouse. IMPORTED SPREADSHEETS NOW COME THROUGH ONE CHECKED DOOR. Bank statements and import sheets arrive from outside the school, so every workbook is now examined before it is read and refused if it tries to alter the program itself. ALSO CARRYING THE PREVIOUS RELEASE, which you never saw a notice for: A REVERSAL NOW ANNOUNCES ITSELF IN THE LEDGER, reading "Reversal of PV-…" instead of repeating the original's wording word for word; reversals already in your books keep their old wording, because a ledger that rewrites its own history is not a ledger. The VAT return states the GRA's split of VAT, NHIL and the GETFund levy beneath the output figure. And going live now requires a recovery code on file — if the only administrator forgets their password, that code is the way back in. THIS RELEASE CARRIES A DATABASE CHANGE. Your figures are untouched, but please back up first: Backup & Export, Back up now.
